title: Blue/Green Sampling + Memory-Aware Quantized Onboarding for Embedding Models
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: New embedding model variants (float16 and memory-quantized) must be introduced without regressions to reranking quality or latency for tenants with varying memory footprints. Our current onboarding relies on tenant-wide canaries and coarse traffic shaping which causes resource spikes or degraded P99 latency when a quantized variant has unexpected memory behavior.

Proposal: Implement a blue/green sampling-based onboarding path combined with a memory-aware quantization profile. Key elements: a shadow prober that samples 1-2% of real requests to the candidate model in blue mode; per-tenant memory heuristics to decide quantization level; gradual green switch with adjustable traffic ramps tied to latency and semantic-similarity signal checks; elastic shard scaling guardrails to prevent OOMs during peak KV cache activity. This will give stronger safety for both quality (semantic regression detection) and latency/cost (memory and compute-aware swaps).
acceptance_criteria: Shadow prober running in blue mode for candidate model across 5 pilot tenants with sampling wheel; results visible in a dashboard
Per-tenant memory heuristic computed and used to choose quantization profile automatically
Automated ramp from blue->green with configurable 1/5/25/50/100% steps and automated rollback if P50/P95/P99 latency or semantic drift thresholds are violated
No increase >5% in end-to-end rerank P99 latency for pilot tenants during progressive switch
Semantic similarity A/B test shows <0.8% degradation in mean reciprocal rank (MRR) for reranking endpoints in pilot tenants
Runbook and rollback steps documented and tested in staging; at least two engineers can execute rollback in <15 minutes
tasks: Design shadow prober component and sampling wheel (ENG-538201-A)
Implement per-tenant memory heuristic service and integrate into model selector (ENG-538201-B)
Add quantization profile mapping and safe-fallback paths (ENG-538201-C)
Extend rollout controller to support blue/green + ramped traffic with automated gates (ENG-538201-D)
Create dashboards: shadow comparisons, semantic-drift signal, memory utilization by tenant, latency SLOs (ENG-538201-E)
Run pilot with 5 tenants for 2 weeks, gather telemetry and tune thresholds (ENG-538201-F)
Document runbook and train on-call handoff for rollout operations (ENG-538201-G)
decisions: Use blue/green shadowing (non-intrusive) instead of immediate canary traffic for first pass to avoid tenant-facing regressions
Adopt three quantization tiers: q8mem (lowest memory), q16perf (balanced), fp16 (baseline) and pick per-tenant based on memory headroom heuristic
Semantic drift detector will use cosine similarity on embedding pairs and a small curated evaluation set per tenant for quicker signal
Automated rollback triggers: +10% P99 latency, -1.5% MRR, or >15% memory headroom reduction events in 5m window
tradeoffs: Blue/green shadowing increases instrumentation and storage for KV cache snapshots — acceptable given reduced customer risk
Per-tenant quantization may slightly complicate billing attribution (different compute vs memory profiles) — will add attribution tags in telemetry
Ramped traffic slows time-to-100% adoption but reduces blast radius and supports targeted tuning per tenant
notes_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting — agreed to pilot with group of existing Dedicated customers that have explicit SLAs and representative memory footprints

2026-03-03: Initial design review with Runtime and Serve teams. Runtime asked for a clear KV cache snapshot schema for shadow runs; Serve asked for ability to bypass shard scaling during shadowing to avoid resource churn

2026-03-04: Prototype shadow prober emitted 1% sampled requests to candidate model; measured end-to-end increase of 0.6% CPU and 0.1% memory when shadowing is enabled cluster-wide (scaled down in pilot)

2026-03-05: Benchmarks on quantized q8mem profile show 35% reduction in peak memory and 18% higher inference latency for 1-token median compared to fp16 — acceptable for tenants with constrained memory but require SLO gate
2026-03-06: PR opened for rollout-controller changes. Pinged UX for ops UI to visualize blue/green lanes and manual override (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rollout/pull/1823)
2026-03-07: Decided threshold tuning: initial ramp waits 30m between steps; rollback if observed trigger in 10m window after step
test_plan: Unit tests for memory heuristic logic and quantization profile selector
Integrations tests that run shadow prober against staging models with synthetic traffic patterns including long-tail sequence lengths
Staging e2e: enable blue/green for synthetic tenant; verify automated ramps and rollback triggers fire under injected latency errors
Pilot A/B: run 5 tenants with shadow enabled for 2 weeks then run ramped adoption for one tenant; validate metrics against acceptance criteria
rollback_plan: Immediate step-down to previous green variant if any rollback trigger detected
If automated rollback fails, manual off-switch in Console to pin tenant to previous model and alert on-call
Evacuate KV cache warm state for affected shards and rehydrate with baseline model to prevent drift
Post-incident: run postmortem and tighten sampling/thresholds before next attempt
monitor_signals: Semantic Drift Score (median cosine similarity vs baseline) and per-tenant MRR delta
Memory headroom percentage by shard and tenant
Shadow v. baseline throughput breakage ratio and error rates
